## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change addresses the reported slider no-op at the right layer. Two points are worth a look: rapid input now spawns unordered `pactl` writes, and the single percentage resets channel balance on every sink.

**Verified** from Quickshell 0.3.1, PipeWire 1.6.8 and `pactl` 17.0 source:

| Step | Before (`audio.volume = v`) | After (`pactl set-sink-volume`) |
|---|---|---|
| Write on a Bluetooth route with no `volumeStep` | `PwNodeBoundAudio::setVolumes` skips the device write (`node.cpp` 489), but still updates `mVolumes` and emits the change, so the slider moves and the server does not | pipewire-pulse writes the card Route param with no `volumeStep` condition (`pulse-server.c` 2792-2835), and bluez5 applies it |
| Scale | Quickshell writes `v^3` linear | `N%` becomes linear `(N/100)^3`, so `Math.round(volume * 100)%` lands on the same value |
| Displayed value | Can disagree with the server | Follows the server through Route param events |

`volumeSink.name` is the Pulse sink name of the same resolved physical sink the volume keys use, and `pactl` (libpulse) is already required by the panel helpers and `omarchy-audio-output-volume`. Current Quickshell master still has the same `volumeStep` gate, so the workaround remains relevant.

### Rapid input spawns unordered, uncoalesced writes

`PanelSlider` emits `moved` on every pointer motion, and each call now starts a separate detached `pactl` process, which is a separate Pulse client. pipewire-pulse applies those writes in arrival order, not launch order. The previous path went through Quickshell's own connection, which kept one Route write outstanding and replaced queued values with the latest one.

`outputVolume` also now updates only after the server round trip, while the bar wheel (`Panel.qml` 648) and keyboard h/l (276) compute `outputVolume + delta`. Conceptual sequence from source, not a measured trace:

```text
wheel +5%  -> outputVolume 50% -> pactl 55%  (in flight)
wheel +5%  -> outputVolume 50% -> pactl 55%  (read-back not yet arrived)
result: 55%, where the previous synchronous setter gave 60%
```

In a private PipeWire 1.6.8 and pipewire-pulse setup with null sinks (synthetic, not a Bluetooth route or a Quickshell session), bursts of six detached `pactl` writes launched about 0.25 ms apart ended on an earlier value in 6 of 20 bursts. At 1.1 ms spacing or more, 0 of 100 bursts did. Spawn to the sink change event took 2.9 to 4.4 ms.

**Impact:** on an idle machine this needs input events only a few milliseconds apart, so it is uncommon. It is more plausible under load, and the released slider or a fast scroll can settle a step away from the intended value. The panel also starts one process per pointer motion event during a drag.

**Suggested change:** use a single `Process` writer where the latest value wins: store the pending percentage, start the process only when idle, and in `onExited` start again only if the pending value differs from the last one sent. Relative steps can then use the pending target as their base instead of `outputVolume`.

### Single percentage resets left/right balance on every sink

`pactl set-sink-volume <sink> N%` with one value sets every channel to `N%` (`pactl.c` `fill_volume`). The previous setter, `setAverageVolume`, scaled each channel by the ratio of requested to current average and kept the balance. The new path applies to all sinks, including ALSA and virtual sinks where the old setter worked.

```text
sink at L 60% / R 40%, panel set to 70%
before: channels scaled, ratio kept
after:  L 70% / R 70%   (observed in the private null-sink setup)
```

**Impact:** affects users who keep an intentionally uneven balance. The volume keys already set a single value the same way (`omarchy-audio-output-volume` 73), so this makes the panel consistent with them rather than introducing a new behavior.

**Suggested change:** make this a deliberate choice. Either note it in the code comment, or pass per-channel values derived from `volumeSink.audio.volumes`, with a fallback to a single value when the channel count does not match.

**Optional test improvement:** the new assertions only match source text. With the `execDetached` line replaced by the comment `// pactl set-sink-volume intentionally removed: no write at all`, the panel performs no write and both assertions still pass. Moving the argv construction into `Model.js` (for example `outputVolumeCommand(name, volume)`) and unit-testing clamping, rounding and the `%` format would test the behavior the assertion message describes.

**Description note:** PipeWire 1.6.8 omits `volumeStep` from a Bluetooth Route only when that transport's hardware volume is not active (`bluez5-device.c` `build_route`), so "all Bluetooth outputs" in the PR description is broader than the actual condition. The code comment states it correctly.

**Related, source reading only:** `setInputVolume` and the Microphone bar widget still assign `source.audio.volume`, which goes through the same `setVolumes` gate. A device-routed Bluetooth input whose Route has no `volumeStep` would likely ignore those controls in the same way. This was not tested.
